belief: God is punishing me with this illness.
origins: Many have heard that sickness is God’s punishment, or they search their past for what they did wrong. Guilt over past sins can attach itself to a diagnosis.
teaches: When Jesus’ disciples asked about a man born blind, “Who sinned, this man or his parents?” Jesus answered, “Neither this man nor his parents sinned, but this happened so that the works of God would be displayed in him.” Job’s friends insisted that his suffering was punishment, and God said they were wrong. “For He knows our frame; He is mindful that we are dust.” Christ bore our sins on the cross: “Surely He took on our infirmities and carried our sorrows.” For the believer, the punishment has been borne. Illness is part of living in a fallen world.
self_statements: God is teaching me a lesson.
My past caught up with me.
errors: Believing God either blesses with health or punishes with illness.
Feeling guilty and concluding that God is punishing me.
questions: What makes me think this is punishment?
How did Jesus answer the question about the blind man?
What does the cross say about my sin?
Do I know faithful people who suffered illness?
What sin, if any, should I bring to God for forgiveness, and is it the cause?
What does God say about me now?
truth: Illness is not God’s punishment for me. Christ carried my sin and sorrows. God is with me in suffering and can display His works even in illness.
hw_truths: There is no condemnation in Christ.
God’s works can be displayed in me.
log: Each week, note one reminder of God’s grace.
actions: Write why you think it is punishment.
Talk with a pastor or counselor.
prayer: Father, I fear You are punishing me. Thank You that Christ bore my sin. Comfort me in this illness and show Your love. Amen.
